references.text: The description of the veil (פָרֹכֶת) that separates the holy place from the Most Holy in the tabernacle, the same veil mentioned in Leviticus 24:3.
The command that the lamp shall burn continuously in the tent of meeting, before the veil, from evening to morning—a parallel command to Leviticus 24:3.
Aaron shall tend the lamps between the two evenings as a perpetual statute (חֻקַּת עוֹלָם)—the same expression and action as in Leviticus 24:3.
Instruction regarding the lampstand and its placement, which complements the description of the lamp service mentioned in Leviticus 24:3.
Reference to the daily lamp service in the temple, a continuation of the service established in Leviticus 24:3.
God's lamp that had not yet gone out in the Lord's temple points to the continuous lamp service commanded in Leviticus 24:3.
The lampstand is placed in the tent of meeting (אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד) opposite the table, and the lamps are lit before the face of the Lord, as described in Leviticus 24:3.
